atoms.b: The British monarchy is a ((controversial)) topic in the UK. Discussions on whether it should continue to exist or be ((abolished)) for good have ((increased)) in recent years, and ((opinions)) on the matter are extremely divided.

instruction.text: Match each opinion with the corresponding speaker.

atoms.a: Royals contribute a lot to helping those in need.

b.sound: I think the monarchy should definitely persist. It's very beneficial for many organisations. Many members of the royal family support charitable causes, such as schools, hospitals and homeless shelters. They are using their wealth for good, I don't see why that should be abolished.

atoms.a: The monarchy is a symbol for British tradition and values.

b.sound: Sure, the royal family both brings in a lot of money and spends it on humanitarian projects, but for me, it's not really about that. The British monarchy is one of the oldest in the world. It's the embodiment of our history and values and should not be lost to modernity.

atoms.a: The economy benefits from the monarchy.

b.sound: The crown is really THE symbol for the UK. This is what the people wanna see! They come here for the atmosphere of antiquity and tradition. Think of all the money generated through tourism, people coming here and buying souvenirs, that would be lost if we got rid of royals entirely.

instruction.text: Match each opinion with the corresponding speaker.

b.sound: The monarchy is just so outdated nowadays. We don't need some symbolic figurehead who isn't even elected by the people. Having an institution like this based on birthright and ancestry perpetuates the idea of social classes and keeps less fortunate people from success.

I always hear the argument that the royals bring in money for the state, but do they really? Why, then, do tax-payers need to pay for their palaces to be maintained, their personal security, and all of that? I think it's about time we use state funds for actually useful projects.

atoms.a: A head of state should be democratically elected.

b.sound: I think it's very problematic someone gets to lead a nation not because of their qualities, but their ancestry. Sure, they don't have any political power in theory, but they can still influence the masses with their actions and opinions. The people should get to choose their head of state.

instruction.text: Read the opinion and answer the question below.

atoms.text: “Sure, the monarchy may not be perfect, but it carries so much symbolic value for our nation. With all the changes happening in our society, the monarchy is a constant presence in our lives. It also reminds us that, as many differences as there are between us, we are all one under the British crown.”

atoms.a: What does the monarchy represent in their opinion? (Multiple answers may be correct.)

instruction.text: Read the opinion and answer the question below.

atoms.text: “I don't really get the attention celebrities get in general, but royals especially get on my nerves. Why are they more important than anyone else? The news is full of every little trivial thing they do. There are real issues out there that deserve media coverage, but instead, I have to see the hundredth report about what the royal family eats for breakfast.”

atoms.a: Which statement best summarises the person's opinion?
b: ++Media reports about royals take away attention from more important topics.
Gossip magazines are annoying and should be banned.
It's exhausting how the news are full of depressing topics.
The monarchy promotes unhealthy eating habits online.

instruction.text: Read the opinion and answer the question below.

atoms.text: “I think it's very important to have a sort of neutral representative of a nation. Politics tend to divide people a lot, even when we all should be standing together. The monarch isn't affiliated with any political party and, therefore, is able to represent all of us equally.”

atoms.a: Which quality of a monarch does the person value?

instruction.text: Read the opinion and answer the question below.

atoms.text: “There are many aspects of British culture to be celebrated, but the crown is not one of them. The monarch's wealth is built on centuries of exploitation, slavery and imperialism kept up by their ancestors. I really don't think we should maintain an institution that has done so much harm all around the world.”

atoms.a: Which statement best summarises the person's opinion?
b: ++The monarchy is a reminder of England's past as a colonial oppressor.
The monarch does not deserve to be this rich.
The monarchy is not an aspect of British culture.
British culture should be celebrated all around.
